reviews.markdown_section:
## First-Run User Review

I walked the new-user path in order against the capture set in `docs/review/2026-10-06-frontend-cobalt/shots/` — landing (01), login modal (02), register modal (03), dashboard light/dark (04/05), then workspace (06/12), project (07/13), ideas wall (08/14), PRD desk (09/15), roadmap (10/16), versions (11/17), profile (18), plus the narrow shots (19/20) — and read the code behind each beat: `landing_page.dart`, `auth_door.dart`, `auth_form.dart`, `dashboard_page.dart`, `app.dart`, `product_dock.dart`, `workspace_page.dart`, `project_page.dart`, `ideas_page.dart`, `prd_desk.dart`, `coach_panel.dart`, `versions_stack.dart`, and the zh/en catalogs. I scored the first three minutes **4/10**.

**What works.** The landing page is the best part of the funnel. The hero ("把想法，一件件打磨出来。") plus one sentence of subtitle tells a new visitor exactly what InsideOut does — capture ideas, let an AI coach grind them into a PRD, split them into a parallel roadmap, and track real commits to delivery — and the four-step assembly story below reinforces it (`landing_page.dart:14-19`). The register modal states the password rule inline. The ideas wall is the strongest in-product surface: the capture input is the visual focus, and the privacy caption ("仅自己可见——想法默认只有作者能看到…") is precisely the reassurance a first-time user needs before typing an unpolished thought. Light and dark themes are coherent across every paired shot, zh/en catalogs are at parity, and the versions page's per-audience readiness checklist is a genuinely good piece of product design. The roadmap empty state tells you what to do next.

**Where it breaks.** The first failure is the chrome. The floating dock renders at the *vertical center* of every signed-in screen, not the bottom: the dashboard chapter paragraph is clipped mid-sentence (04/05), the workspace delete row is half-hidden (06/12), and the versions checklist's last two items are unreadable (11/17). The cause is in `product_dock.dart:26-29`: the widget returns `SafeArea(child: Center(...))` and `AppScaffold` (app.dart:135) inserts it as `Scaffold.bottomNavigationBar` — a `Center` expands to fill the loose height the Scaffold offers, so the nav bar silently becomes full-height and the pill centers in it. The intended `static const height = 88.0` exists but is never referenced. This one bug also explains why the workspace page's create-project FAB (its only creation affordance, `workspace_page.dart:115-118`) is nowhere in shots 06/12: the FAB anchors relative to a nav bar whose top is at the viewport top. A new user in a fresh workspace quite literally cannot start a project.

The dock also teaches unreliability. `DockItem.evidence` unconditionally calls `stay()` (product_dock.dart:129-130) — a labeled navigation button that is a guaranteed no-op with no toast, no disabled state. `DockItem.version` navigates to `/prd/$prd`, which is the page already open when you're on the desk — another silent dead click (captures.md A6). On top of that, the "unfinished" nudge replaces the 提交 label with the longer "未完成：提交", which overflows its slot and lands as a white pill on the icon (10/18) — designed behavior that reads as a stuck tooltip.

Information architecture adds friction. The project page headlines itself "证据" in the largest type, with the actual project name demoted beneath (`project_page.dart:150-155`), so a user who clicked "Onboarding Revamp" can't confirm where they are. The workspace page is four label-only rows — 想法 / 设置 / 编辑 / 删除这个工作区 — with no chevron and no description, and the destructive row is styled identically to the neutral ones (A7); FieldCard has no trailing affordance at all. The dashboard hides "create workspace" once you have one (the button only exists in the empty state, `dashboard_page.dart:231-247`). The auth modal card itself is untitled: the disc, "InsideOut", and the "登录/创建账号" greeting are siblings *above* the card in a centered Column (`auth_door.dart:50-71`), which is why the wordmark floats over the landing hero and collides with the 开始打磨/登录 buttons in shot 02 (the lead reviewer's confirmed defect) — and even when it doesn't collide, the greeting is 12px bodySmall dark text on a black54 scrim.

Data surfaces feel half-finished. The updates feed shows a raw English enum chip ("progress") and a raw ISO timestamp (`project_page.dart:304-307`) while the workspace card two screens away renders "进展 · 8 小时前" from the same data — the l10n keys exist. The PRD desk shows three big section cards with no body, no placeholder, and borderless fields (`prd_desk.dart:96-107`), so the first-run user has no idea the coach's questions are meant to be answered there. The versions readiness list mixes languages on one line: localized section name + raw server English gloss (`versions_stack.dart:184`). Smaller wobbles: clicking an idea card's title or body does nothing (only the tiny PRD chip works); the invite banner's hint ends in a dangling colon; "大段引语" renders as a permanent subtitle under the coach title with nothing beneath it; the cryptic manifesto line "没有标签，也没有文件夹。" floats centered below the only idea card.

**What I would do first.** Fix the dock layout: bound `bottomNavigationBar` to the already-defined 88px height and bottom-align the pill. That single change clears the content overlap on every screen, restores the create-project FAB, and makes the existing per-page bottom padding actually meaningful. Immediately after, wire the two silent dock dead clicks and the idea-card tap, re-run the sim walk in `scripts/sim`, and only then take the copy/IA pass (project heading, dashboard labels, destructive-row styling). The bones of a trustworthy product are visible on the landing page and ideas wall; the chrome between them is currently spending that trust faster than the screens earn it back.

reviews.bottom_line: The current UI is a coherent, well-disciplined execution of the *rounded* Cobalt card lock — and that is precisely the problem: against the Cobalt-Neo target it fails all four structural pillars. There is no shadow system at all (elevation is explicitly zeroed and the only two shadows in the app are soft Material blurs), every radius token (12/20/28/999) is the exact inverse of the 0px decree, container borders are 1px periwinkle hairlines instead of 2px, and no press-the-block interaction or 100ms motion token exists anywhere. The cobalt palette itself is faithfully and cleanly tokenized, and dark/light parity is real — so the migration is a token-layer rebuild, not a rewrite. Score 2.5/10 against the Cobalt-Neo target.
strengths: One-hue cobalt palette kept and centrally tokenized: client/lib/theme/cobalt.dart:62-66 defines hue50-hue950; the pre-built code map found zero withOpacity/fromRGBO and only 5 hardcoded color lines across all of client/lib.
True dark/light parity from a single class: cobalt.dart:102-154 mirrors every semantic key; shots 05-dashboard-dark and 09-prd-desk-dark render consistently with their light twins 04/15.
Ideas-wall display type matches the lock spec clamp(64px,10vw,320px): ideas_page.dart:181-192, visible in shots 08/14.
Cobalt-500 on white measures 5.09:1 (computed) — primary buttons pass WCAG AA; btn/btnFg pairing is disciplined in both themes (cobalt.dart:117-118, 144-145).
Chrome consistency: the capture-to-evidence bottom dock renders identically on every signed-in surface (shots 04-11, 16-17), matching DESIGN.md's loop-navigation intent.

findings.summary: The four radius tokens are 12/20/28/999 — every control class (buttons, inputs, chips, cards, dock, modal) ships rounded, the exact inverse of the 0px-by-decree target, and features add hardcoded radii on top.
findings.failure_scenario: Shots 01/02/08/14/16 show pills on every button and input, 20px cards, a 28px modal, a circular brand disc, and a StadiumBorder capture bar (ideas_page.dart:200) — none of which can survive the 0px decree; a token-by-token swap is unavoidable and touches ~20 call sites plus hardcoded radii (step_peek.dart:65 circular(99), roadmap_node_card.dart:83 circular(99), versions_stack.dart:113 vertical top 10, roadmap_canvas.dart:194/204/216).

findings.summary: There is no press-the-block interaction anywhere: no hover state, no shadow-shrink-plus-translate, no 100ms motion token — the only motion system is a 650ms expo ease for mount reveals, and the lone MouseRegion in the app is the roadmap canvas cursor tracker.

findings.failure_scenario: The target's core feel — hover: shadow 4px→2px + translate(2,2); active: shadow gone + translate(4,4); 100ms — cannot be implemented per-widget without a shared token, so each developer will invent different durations/curves; today's UI gives only the Material ink splash (FieldCard's InkWell, field_card.dart:35-39) and an unrelated 180ms fade on dock selection (product_dock.dart:162).
findings.fix: Define motion tokens in Cobalt (pressDuration 100ms, pressCurve, hoverShadow 2px, hoverOffset (2,2), activeOffset (4,4), disabled rule) and ship one shared InkWell/ButtonStyle extension implementing the shadow+translate swap; convert FieldCard, buttons, dock items, and node cards to it.

reviews.markdown_section:
## Design-Fidelity Review — Cobalt-Neo Migration Gap Analysis

I compared the shipped Flutter client against the Cobalt-Neo target (0px radius, 2px container borders, hard 4px 4px 0 0 offset shadows, press-the-block interactions at 100ms, dark-first neutral gray ramp, cobalt-#3B5BFF palette retained). Evidence came from a full read of `client/lib/theme/cobalt.dart`, `cobalt_theme.dart`, `field_card.dart`, `cobalt_chip.dart`, `ink_motion.dart`, `chrome/product_dock.dart`, `features/auth/auth_door.dart`, `session/appearance.dart`, and `features/prd/coach_panel.dart`; `DESIGN.md`, `docs/design-system/cobalt/README.md`, and `docs/design-system/CHANGELOG.md`; the reference neo-brutalist brief; the pre-built code map; nine screenshots across both themes (01, 02, 04, 05, 08, 09, 14, 16 plus the capture index); and computed WCAG contrast ratios for every relevant token pair. A repo-wide grep confirmed there is no existing neo/brutalist mention anywhere — the migration spec is genuinely greenfield.

**What is already right.** The palette half of the contract is in excellent shape. `cobalt.dart:62-66` defines the hue50–hue950 ramp once, both themes mirror every semantic key (`cobalt.dart:102-154`), and the code map's token-discipline pass found almost no color bypasses — five hardcoded lines in features, zero `withOpacity`/`fromRGBO`. Cobalt-500 on white computes to 5.09:1, so primary actions pass AA today. Dark and light genuinely parity: shots 05/09 and 04/15 are faithful twins. The ideas-wall display type implements the lock's `clamp(64px,10vw,320px)` spec exactly (`ideas_page.dart:181-192`), and the bottom dock gives every signed-in surface consistent loop chrome. The failure is not execution quality — it is that the executed design is the wrong design.

**Finding 1 — there is no shadow system (Critical).** The `Cobalt` class contains no shadow or elevation tokens of any kind, and the theme suppresses the Material defaults: `cardTheme` has `elevation: 0` (`cobalt_theme.dart:56`), the AppBar has `elevation: 0` (:49). The only two shadows in the entire app are soft, blurred Material elevations — the auth modal (`auth_door.dart:79-80`, elevation 6, black at 35% alpha) and the dock (`product_dock.dart:31`, elevation 8). The neo-brutalist signature is an unblurred `4px 4px 0 0` cast on every container, and there is no substrate to hang it on. This matters beyond aesthetics: with 0px radius and 2px borders but no cast shadow, boxes go flat. I computed the current dark-mode surface separation — raised-on-base is 1.09:1, sunken-on-base 1.42:1, stroke-on-raised 1.45:1 — so in dark mode cards already barely separate from the page, and the reference system solves that with shadows plus border weight, not contrast.

**Finding 2 — the radius decree is inverted (Critical).** `cobalt.dart:72-75` defines `radiusControl = 12.0`, `radiusCard = 20.0`, `radiusHero = 28.0`, `radiusPill = 999.0`. Buttons, FilledButtons, text inputs, chips, the FAB, and the dock are pills by theme wiring (`cobalt_theme.dart:28-33`, `87-111`); FieldCard is 20px everywhere (`field_card.dart:28`); the auth card is 28px; the capture bar is a literal `StadiumBorder` (`ideas_page.dart:200`); and features hardcode further radii — `circular(99)` twice, top-radius 10 on the versions stack, and 12/4/3/1px corners on the roadmap canvas. Every shot confirms it: 01, 02, 08, 14, and 16 are a sea of pills. Against a 0px-by-decree target this is the single widest-scoped change.

**Finding 3 — no press-the-block interaction exists (Critical).** The target's feel is hover: shadow 4→2px + translate(2,2); active: shadow gone + translate(4,4); 100ms. I grepped the whole client: the only `MouseRegion` is the roadmap canvas's remote-cursor tracker. Tappables get Material's default ink splash (`field_card.dart:35-39`) and one unrelated 180ms selection fade on the dock (`product_dock.dart:162`). The motion file (`ink_motion.dart`) is a mount-reveal system — 650ms expo ease — philosophically opposite to fast mechanical press motion, and there are no duration/curve/offset tokens to implement the target with.

**Findings 4–6 — borders, dark ramp, theme default (High).** Every container border is a default-width 1.0px `BorderSide` in cobalt-200 (`field_card.dart:29`), a 1.49:1 hairline in light mode; focused inputs and the dock's unfinished outline are already 1.5px, so widths drift. The dark ramp is blue-tinted — ground `#0B0D12`, raised `#141820`, sunken literally `hue950` (`#1E2A5A`) — not the neutral `#000/#111/#1A1A1A/#222 + #333 border` ladder, and shot 05 shows three near-identical navy blacks where elevation should be. And the app is light-first: `Appearance({..., this.dark = false})` (`appearance.dart:36`) with no `prefers-color-scheme` fallback — the inverse of the dark-first requirement.

**Findings 7–12 (Medium/Low).** Status semantics are cobalt washes — `statusSuccessBg: hue50`, `statusWarnBg: hue200`, `fgDanger: hue700` (`cobalt.dart:116-126`) — so done/warning/danger differ only by cobalt step, and the app's only true red is a hardcoded `#B3261E` in `admin_section.dart:167`. The coach panel is an off-ladder always-dark navy built on `Cobalt.hue950` with dark mode detected by `surfaceBase == Cobalt.darkGround` identity (`coach_panel.dart:111-112, 231`) — visible staying navy in light shot 15. Light-mode wells are brand-tinted (`surfaceSunken: hue50`). There is no 4px spacing scale, both body roles are 17.5px, and paddings are per-widget ad hoc. The dark shadow color is undefined (the dock hand-rolls 18% lightInk). And `DESIGN.md:27-45` still prescribes the rounded lock — it even disagrees with code (doc control radius 9999px vs `radiusControl` 12.0) — so the documented contract will fight the migration until rewritten alongside a CHANGELOG 2.0.0 major bump.

**What I would do first.** Nothing above can be coded until the values exist. Draft the Cobalt-Neo token table — dark and light gray ramps, border widths (2px container / 1px divider), cast and pressed shadows with an explicit dark-mode shadow color, press-motion tokens (100ms, offsets, curve), the semantic-hue policy, the type/spacing scale decision, and the dark-first default — as a dated reviewed plan, then land it as `Cobalt` 2.0.0 with the theme-level widgets (FieldCard, ShadeChip, AuthDoor, ProductDock, button/input themes) converted before any feature screen is touched.

reviews.bottom_line: The Cobalt token system is fundamentally sound for body text — every foreground/background pair I computed passes WCAG AA in both light and dark (4.55:1 to 18.29:1) — but the chrome around it fails badly: the dock's 'unfinished step' state is 1.32:1 blue-on-blue in light theme, the floating top-bar icons are 1.42:1 over the navy coach panel on the PRD page, every stroke/border token sits at 1.40–2.26:1 against WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1, and the roadmap minimap encodes status as unlabeled 4px color marks at 1.40–2.90:1. There is no focus strategy anywhere in client/lib (zero focusColor/FocusNode usages), text ships at 9–11px in three places, and the known brightness-sniff in coach_panel.dart is both fragile (color identity) and currently a no-op ternary whose two branches resolve to identical colors. Score 4.5/10: a strong type/contrast foundation undermined by systemic non-text contrast failures on primary navigation.

findings.summary: The dock's 'unfinished step' cue paints icon, 11px label, and 1.5px border in the warn token on the cobalt dock — 1.32:1 in light theme, 3.41:1 in dark.
findings.failure_scenario: The primary navigation's only 'you skipped the human commit step' signal is invisible in light theme (blue on cobalt) and below the 4.5:1 body-text bar in dark; users never learn the loop is incomplete, and the A5 stuck-badge behavior makes it worse.
findings.fix: Introduce an on-brand warn token (e.g. #FFD166 amber: ~7:1 on hue500) or drop the warn color on the pill entirely and mark unfinished steps with a white dot + tooltip; recompute with the same WCAG script until ≥4.5:1.

findings.summary: The floating utility icons (language/theme/profile/logout) have no backdrop and render dark-on-navy — 1.42:1 — wherever a page's dark content reaches the top strip, e.g. the PRD coach panel in light theme.
findings.failure_scenario: A light-theme user on /prd/:id cannot see the theme toggle, profile, or logout buttons (1.42:1); the same layering will break on any future full-bleed dark surface.
findings.fix: Give the utilities Row a surfaceRaised/95% background pill (or hoist a real AppBar with backgroundColor) so icon color always pairs with a known surface; add a golden screenshot asserting ≥3:1 for those icons.

findings.summary: All four stroke tokens are 1.40–2.26:1 against their surfaces — every card border, input border, outlined button, chip border, and divider in the app fails the 3:1 non-text minimum.
findings.failure_scenario: Low-vision users cannot perceive form field boundaries (1.49:1 on white) — the entire auth flow and every editor input — or card edges; the light-theme UI reads as borderless gray mush.
findings.fix: Retune stroke tokens to ≥3:1 (light strokeStrong ≈ #6E7FD6, light strokeSubtle ≈ #94A3E8; dark strokeSubtle ≈ #4A5680); the WCAG python script already in this review becomes the regression check.

findings.summary: The roadmap minimap encodes node status as unlabeled 4px color bars whose colors fail 3:1 — locked 1.40:1, pending 2.18:1 (light) — so status is conveyed by color alone, mostly invisibly, on a navigation control.
findings.failure_scenario: On a project with locked/pending nodes, the minimap shows nothing at all (marks nearly identical to the page ground); colorblind users can't distinguish done vs in-progress even where marks are visible — band status is only in color.
findings.fix: Raise mark colors to ≥3:1 vs surface and add a non-color channel: filled bar = done, hollow (bordered) = pending, hatched/dashed = locked, or an aria-style Semantics label + tooltip per column.

findings.summary: Error text uses a literal Color(0xFFB3261E) instead of the theme's fgDanger, giving 2.72:1 in dark mode against surfaceRaised #141820 (theme token would give 13.03:1).
findings.failure_scenario: Admin-facing failure messages (invite/revoke errors) are unreadable in dark theme exactly when the operator needs them most.
findings.fix: Replace the literal with Theme.of(context).colorScheme.error (or palette.fgDanger) and add a lint banning Color(0x outside theme/.

findings.summary: Grep finds zero focusColor, zero FocusNode, zero focus-highlight customization anywhere in client/lib — keyboard focus relies on Material defaults, which on the cobalt dock compute to ~1.3:1, and the dock's selected state is a 1.31:1 white wash.

## Accessibility & Visual Review — Cobalt Frontend

I reviewed the theme system and its application across the product: `client/lib/theme/cobalt.dart` (palette tokens) and `cobalt_theme.dart` (ThemeData wiring, type roles) read in full; every other widget file cross-referenced through the pre-built code map; all 20 in-app screenshots in `docs/review/2026-10-06-frontend-cobalt/shots/` inspected at native resolution; and WCAG 2.x contrast ratios computed with a python3 script over every meaningful foreground/background pair in both themes. I also grepped `client/lib` for `fontSize:`, `Focus`/`focusColor`/`focusNode`/`autofocus`, `Color(0x` literals, `Semantics`, and `textScaler` overrides. Findings below are mine alone; the two lead-confirmed defects (auth-modal header collision, dock overlaying body content) are cited only where they intersect accessibility.

### What is genuinely good

The type-and-color foundation is better than most design systems I review. Every body-text token pair passes WCAG AA in both themes, computed: fgPrimary/surface 18.29:1 (both themes), fgSecondary 9.93:1 light / 11.81:1 dark, fgMuted 4.55:1 light / 6.28:1 dark, button text on brand 5.09:1 light / 4.79:1 dark, dark fgBrand 13.03:1. Tooltips are on every chrome icon button. The motion layer honors `MediaQuery.disableAnimations` (`ink_motion.dart:6`). Nothing overrides text scaling. CJK fallback chains are declared so zh-CN never tofu. Only six hardcoded color literals exist outside `theme/`, most of them the locked brand hue. And the focused input border is explicitly styled (`cobalt_theme.dart:100-103`) — the one place keyboard-adjacent states got real design attention.

### Critical

**Dock "unfinished" cue is blue-on-cobalt (1.32:1 light / 3.41:1 dark).** `product_dock.dart:166,172,177` paints the icon, the 11px label, and a 1.5px border in `statusWarnFg` on the brand-colored pill. In light theme both are blues from the same ramp — `#1D4ED8` on `#3B5BFF` — and the result is invisible in `10-roadmap-dark.png` and would be worse in light. This is the product's only "you skipped the human commit step" signal, on its primary navigation. It needs an on-brand warn token (amber clears 7:1 on hue500) or a shape/position treatment instead of color.

**Top-bar icons float with no backdrop (1.42:1 on the PRD page).** `app.dart:90-130` positions the language/theme/profile/logout `IconButton`s in a bare `Positioned` row; the coach panel fills the right column full-bleed with navy `hue950` even in light theme (`coach_panel.dart:112`), so in light mode those icons render `#0B0D12` on `#1E2A5A`. Shot `15-prd-desk-light.png` shows all four effectively gone — theme toggle, profile, and logout unreachable for light-theme users on `/prd/:id`. Give the strip a surface background pill or a real AppBar.

### High

**Every stroke token fails WCAG 1.4.11 (1.40–2.26:1).** `strokeSubtle`/`strokeStrong` (`cobalt.dart:109-110,136-137`) are used for input borders, card borders, outlined buttons, chip borders, and dividers — so form boundaries are 1.49:1 on white (see the login modal's near-outline-less fields in `02-login-modal.png`) and card edges are 1.40–2.26:1 everywhere. Low-vision users will read the light UI as borderless. Retune to ≥3:1.

**Roadmap minimap: color-only, mostly invisible status.** `roadmap_canvas.dart:172-183` draws unlabeled 4px bars per node status using outline tokens — locked 1.40:1, pending 2.18:1 (light), done 2.90:1 (dark). The control encodes state purely by color, and the colors fail the 3:1 graphics floor; on a project with locked/pending nodes the minimap shows nothing at all. Raise contrast and add a non-color channel (filled/hollow/hatched) plus tooltips.

**Admin error red bypasses the theme (2.72:1 dark).** `admin_section.dart:167` hardcodes `Color(0xFFB3261E)` where the theme already ships a dark-safe `fgDanger` (13.03:1). The literal is unreadable on dark `surfaceRaised`.

### Medium

**No focus strategy exists.** Grep finds zero `focusColor`, zero `FocusNode`, no focus styling anywhere; only `Focus(autofocus: true)` for Esc handling in the auth modal and one autofocus on the login field. Material's default ~12% primary-tint focus overlay on the cobalt dock computes to ~1.3:1, and the dock's selected state is a 1.31:1 white alpha wash (`product_dock.dart:165`) — so neither focus location nor current route is perceivable keyboard-only.

**Dark-theme status pills collapse into one color.** `cobalt.dart:142-153` sets dark `fgDanger`, `statusInfoFg`, `statusWarnFg`, `statusSuccessFg` all to hue200 on identical hue950 backgrounds — danger text is hex-identical to informational accents. Light warn pill is 4.49:1, one-hundredth under AA at its 12px semibold size.

**The brightness sniff is fragile and a no-op.** `coach_panel.dart:230-232` defines `brightnessIsDark => surfaceBase == Cobalt.darkGround` — a palette identity check — and the ternary it feeds resolves both branches to identical colors (`#F7F8FA`/`#1E2A5A` either way). It works today by accident and will silently break the first time someone retunes the dark palette. `Theme.of(context).brightness` is right there in `Cobalt.of`.

**Text ships at 9–11px.** Remote-cursor names at 10px (`roadmap_canvas.dart:100`), minimap labels at 9px clipped to six characters (`:226`), and every dock button's only label at 11px (`product_dock.dart:178`).

### Low

Brand hue500 on dark surfaces reaches only 3.82:1 as large display text (the ideas-wall title, `ideas_page.dart:191`) and 2.69:1 as graphics (presence-cursor icons, coach accent bar) — a dark-theme parity break. The coach input hint at 50% alpha computes 4.37:1. Both are near-misses with cheap token fixes.

### What I would do first

Fix the tokens before any widget work: retune `strokeSubtle/strokeStrong`, add a true dark danger red, an on-brand warn color, and a `brandOnDark`, all verified by a checked-in Dart contrast test that recomputes these ratios in CI. That single file (`cobalt.dart`) plus `product_dock.dart`'s warn/selected colors clears the widest-reaching failures — borders, the unfinished cue, the selected wash — everywhere at once, and converts this system's genuinely strong text contrast into chrome that low-vision and keyboard users can actually operate.

Beyond that, the web index.html is missing the viewport meta tag, the coach panel and roadmap canvas reserve no bottom space for the dock, several dialogs/sections use fixed pixel sizes that overflow at 390px, and mobile coverage exists for only 2 of 13 routes. Desktop >=900px code discipline (Expanded, Wrap, breakpoints) is good, but shipped responsive behavior is broken at every width.

## Responsive/Overflow Reviewer

### What I examined

I read the app chrome (`client/lib/app.dart`, `client/lib/chrome/product_dock.dart`), every page-level layout file (`dashboard_page.dart`, `workspace_page.dart`, `project_page.dart`, `ideas_page.dart`, `prd_page.dart`, `roadmap_page.dart`, `versions_stack.dart`, `versions_commit_dialog.dart`, `coach_panel.dart`, `field_card.dart`), the web host file (`client/web/index.html`, `client/lib/main.dart`), the local Flutter 3.44.8 SDK sources for `Scaffold` and `RenderPositionedBox` layout behavior, the pre-built code map, and the capture index. I personally inspected shots 04, 06, 09, 11, 16, 19, 20, and 21 at full resolution; the remaining desktop shots are corroborated by the capture index (A2). Mobile coverage at 390px exists only for dashboard (19), ideas wall (20), and the resize anomaly (21) — a gap I flag as a finding in itself.

### The confirmed defect, with its real root cause

The lead-confirmed defect — "at 1440x900 the bottom dock overlays dashboard body content" — is real but misdiagnosed by its symptom. The dock does not sit at the bottom at all. In shot 04 the pill is centered at approximately (720, 440) of a 1440x900 viewport; in the narrow shots 19/20 it is centered at approximately (390, 825) of 780x1688 — in both cases the vertical midpoint of the screen, with a large empty band below. Shot 21 shows the same mid-screen placement after resize.

The cause is a three-part chain. `AppScaffold` passes the dock as `bottomNavigationBar: signedIn ? const ProductDock() : null` (`client/lib/app.dart:135`) on a `Scaffold` with `extendBody: true` (`app.dart:71`). `ProductDock.build` returns `SafeArea(minimum: EdgeInsets.fromLTRB(16, 0, 16, 16), child: Center(child: Material(...)))` (`client/lib/chrome/product_dock.dart:26-28`). The Scaffold's own layout delegate (`scaffold.dart:1035,1049-1052` in the SDK) lays out the bottomNavigationBar with `fullWidthConstraints` — width tightened to the viewport, height bounded to it. `Center` is `Align` with no factors, and `RenderPositionedBox.performLayout` only shrink-wraps when `constraints.maxHeight == double.infinity`; here it is finite, so the `Center` expands to the full 900px and vertically centers the pill inside it. The 900px-tall bottomNavigationBar is then positioned at `bottom - height = 0`, so the pill lands at the viewport's vertical center on every signed-in route. The correct minimal fix is `Align(alignment: Alignment.bottomCenter, heightFactor: 1.0)` — the `heightFactor` restores shrink-wrap — after which the pill truly anchors at the bottom and every page's `bottom: 140` padding starts meaning what it was written to mean.

### Strengths worth keeping

The code underneath the bug is more disciplined than the rendering suggests. There is a single breakpoint convention — `MediaQuery.sizeOf(context).width >= 900` at `dashboard_page.dart:134`, `prd_page.dart:153`, `assembly_step.dart:33` — and narrow branches genuinely exist (dashboard cards stack at `dashboard_page.dart:171-175`; the PRD split becomes a stacked ListView at `prd_page.dart:165-169`). Button groups on the project page use `Wrap` (`project_page.dart:162-180`), which cannot overflow horizontally. The ideas-wall grid math at `ideas_page.dart:239` — `(width - 88) / 3`, `(width - 72) / 2`, `width - 56` — is exactly self-consistent with its ListView's 56px horizontal padding at both breakpoints. `FieldCard` clips (`field_card.dart:31`), which safely contains the idea poster's deliberately off-edge decorative circle (`ideas_page.dart:292-302`). `SafeArea` is used for the dock, the top-right utilities, and the auth modal, and the display type is fluid via a clamp (`cobalt.dart:97`).

### Findings walkthrough (severity order)

Beyond re-rooting the dock defect, the High items are latent or host-level. The coach panel (`coach_panel.dart:129`, bottom padding 8) and the roadmap canvas view (`roadmap_page.dart:176` header bottom 8, canvas `Expanded` with no clearance) are the only full-height surfaces with no dock clearance; today this is masked by the floating dock, but once the pill is bottom-anchored the coach's input row and the canvas bottom will sit under it — these must land in the same change set as the dock fix.
